review_notes: Read the whole target file, plus Def_NumberField_NormPowChar, Def_AutomorphicForm_EtaFamily and the relevant part of Def_NumberField_TateGlobalZeta. I checked which simp attributes exist on the lemmas the file uses (cpowChar_apply_val is simp; normPowChar_eq_one_of_ideleNorm_eq_one, mem_normOneIdeles_iff and etaFst_apply are not). I found no rewrite cycle and no competing rules. Both findings are about missing simp-interface lemmas, and I did not run Lean. Whether simp would discharge the side condition in the second finding is untested.

findings.declaration: solution (local ψf definition and its repeated unfolding)
findings.problem: The local `let ψf` (a `Sum.elim` whose `inl` branch is a `dite` on `∃ i', em₂ i' = em₁ i`) has no simp lemmas of its own. Every goal that mentions `ψf (Sum.inl i)` therefore unfolds the definition by hand with `simp only [ψf, Sum.elim_inl, dif_pos h]` or `dif_neg h`. This appears about 19 times (lines 493–668), several times with extra lemmas, and it exposes `h.choose` instead of a named normal form. The unfolding is tied to the definition's internal shape. The proof also needs `show`/`rfl` steps for `φf`/`ψf` at lines 548–549, 585–587 and 666.
findings.proposed_change: Right after defining `ψf`, prove two local equations and use them in place of the repeated unfolding. They would be `hψf_pos : ∀ i (h : ∃ i', em₂ i' = em₁ i) s g, ψf (Sum.inl i) s g = ψf₂ h.choose (s + ((τ₁ i - τ₂ h.choose : ℝ) : ℂ) * Complex.I) g := by intros; simp [ψf, dif_pos h]` and `hψf_neg : ∀ i, ¬ ∃ i', em₂ i' = em₁ i → ∀ s g, ψf (Sum.inl i) s g = 0`. Add `hψf_inr : ψf (Sum.inr t) = ψf₂ t.1` and `hφf_inr : φf (Sum.inr t) s g = 0`, also proved by `rfl`. Each case can then use `rw [hψf_pos i h]` or `simp [hψf_pos i h]`. The unfolding of `ψf` appears once, and the branches no longer depend on the `Sum.elim`/`dite` shape.
findings.benefit: The 19 near-identical unfolding steps become one-line rewrites with named lemmas. The proof is easier to read, and a change to `ψf` only needs the three lemmas updated.

findings.excerpt: rw [MonoidHom.mul_apply, normPowChar_eq_one_of_ideleNorm_eq_one τ ((mem_normOneIdeles_iff z).1 hz), mul_one]
findings.problem: The normalising rewrites for `normPowChar` have no simp interface. `normPowChar_eq_one_of_ideleNorm_eq_one` takes the hypothesis `ideleNorm F x = 1`, and the membership predicate `x ∈ normOneIdeles F` is turned into it only by the non-simp `mem_normOneIdeles_iff`. So each use manually converts `hz` with `(mem_normOneIdeles_iff z).1 hz` and chains `rw` (lines 86, 90–91), and clients repeat this (the call sites at lines 3 to 4 in h1μ..h2ν use `rw; exact`). `normPowChar_zero` is not marked simp either. The shift lemmas `etaFst_mul_normPowChar'` and `etaSnd_mul_normPowChar_inv'` have the orientation simp would want, since they eliminate `normPowChar`. They are only used by `rw`, and `etaFst_apply`/`etaSnd_apply` are not simp, so their proofs have to unfold everything with long explicit `rw` lists (lines 64–66, 75–78). The primed names for these lemmas also recur in other P2M/Sol files.
findings.proposed_change: Mark `mem_normOneIdeles_iff` as `@[simp]`, or add `normPowChar_apply_of_mem : z ∈ normOneIdeles F → normPowChar F t z = 1`, and tag it and `normPowChar_zero` with `@[simp]`. Tag `mul_normPowChar_apply_of_mem` and `mul_normPowChar_inv_apply_of_mem` as `@[simp]`, so that `(χ * normPowChar K τ) z` rewrites to `χ z` when `hz` is in the context. These lemmas are stated for any `χ`, so they would sit better next to `normPowChar` in Def_NumberField_NormPowChar than in this solution file. Give the two shift lemmas one canonical home and `@[simp]` there, instead of the primed copies in several solution files. Then h1μ, h1ν, h2μ and h2ν could be closed with `by simp [(_hem₁ i).1, hz]`.
findings.benefit: Callers can discharge `normPowChar` and its inverse with plain `simp` instead of building the `ideleNorm = 1` witness by hand. There would be one canonical normal form (no `normPowChar` factor on norm-one ideles, a shifted `s` in `etaFst`/`etaSnd`) instead of lemma copies in several files.
